title: Streamline verification & publishing flow with rollback metrics for performance profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Publishing a Redwood-verified performance profile today is a multi-step manual handoff across research, infra, and runtime teams. We lack clear rollback thresholds and automated invalidation when observed production telemetry deviates from the profile. This increases risk when pinning customer deployments to newly onboarded model versions.

Goal: Define and implement a streamlined verification -> publish -> monitor -> rollback flow for performance profiles that produces a machine-readable profile artifact, enforces deterministic naming and pin semantics, and attaches actionable rollback metrics. The flow should reduce manual steps, provide clear canary windows, and enable automated alerts/partial rollbacks when SLAs regress beyond tolerance.

Scope (what success looks like):
- A documented publish workflow and Confluence playbook for engineers/PMs that ties into the existing onboarding pipeline.
- A new profile artifact format (JSONL metadata + canonical test harness ID) with versioning and immutable checksum.
- CI checks and a runtime gating step that validates profiles against a staged canary for 1-2 hours before marking them "verified".
- Telemetry-driven rollback rules (P95 latency + throughput loss + cost delta) that can trigger automated rollback or create high-priority incidents.

Out of scope: full UI polish in Console (we'll ship a minimal Console toggle + affordance), long-term storage retention policy changes (handled by another project).
acceptance_criteria: Publish playbook published in Confluence with step-by-step runbook and broken-out responsibilities
Profile artifact schema v1 defined and checked into github.com/redwood/profiles-schema as profiles-v1.json
CI gating passes for new profiles: schema validation, checksum verification, integration test id present
Canary gating implemented: a staged traffic policy runs for a configurable window (default 60m) and emits pass/fail based on configured thresholds

Rollback rules defined and implemented in runtime: if observed P95 latency increases by >25% AND throughput drops >15% for the same workload, mark profile unverified and route traffic to pinned fallback
Console shows verified/unverified state and a link to canary telemetry dashboard (minimal UI accepted for MVP)
Automation test that flips a profile to unverified when synthetic traffic reproduces regression (end-to-end test in CI)
tasks: Define profile artifact schema and versioning scheme (owner: Eng infra)
Add schema validation step to onboarding CI (owner: Eng)
Implement canary gating control in deployment pipeline (owner: Runtime)
Create standard rollback rule templates and thresholds (owner: PM + Runtime)
Add telemetry dashboards for canary runs: latency P50/P95, tokens/sec, cost-per-token baseline (owner: Observability)
Wire Console to show verified status + quick rollback button (owner: Console, minimal MVP)
Draft Confluence playbook and runbook with escalation path (owner: PM)
Run 3 pilot onboards with the new flow and collect feedback (owners: Research, Runtime, PM)
notes: Decision: Profiles will be immutable once marked verified; new versions must have incremented semver and new checksum

Trade-off discussed: tighter thresholds reduce surface-area for performance regressions but increase false-positive rollbacks; settled on conservative default thresholds with ability to tune per-model
Format decision: JSONL header with keys: model_id, profile_version, checksum, ci_build_id, canonical_harness_id, latency_baselines, throughput_baselines, cost_estimates
Security: Since profile artifacts include no customer data, we can store them in the internal artifact registry; however publishing must require a signed CI token (security review required)
